questions.title: Which country will become the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords by September 27, 2026?
questions.background: The Artemis Accords establish principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from NASA or the U.S. Department of State, or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution : Resolve to the country that becomes the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords on or before September 27, 2026. A completed signing is required; an expression of interest or an intention to sign does not qualify. A signing after that deadline does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 2026, 67 nations have signed the Artemis Accords (Paraguay became #67 on May 7, 2026, following 2026 signings by Portugal, Oman, Latvia, Jordan, Morocco, Malta, and Ireland). Reaching #75 by September 27 (coinciding with UNGA High-Level Week) requires eight additional signings from 40+ plausible non-signatory U.S.-aligned states, so predicting which exact country lands specifically on slot #75 is highly diffuse—each leading candidate carries roughly a 4–6% marginal probability, and proper Brier Skill Score optimization requires not inflating top-5 probabilities. Top non-signatory candidates based on regional waves and U.S. space ties include Croatia (the sole remaining EU member state not yet signed), Qatar (following Oman, Jordan, and Morocco in the Arab world), Costa Rica (leading Latin American holdout), Kenya (top East African space partner), and Indonesia (largest ASEAN holdout after Malaysia and the Philippines signed).

questions.title: Who will score the match-winning goal in Portugal's opening fixture of the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League?
questions.background: Portugal enter the competition as defending champions. This question concerns their senior men's team's first league-phase match.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official match report or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera Sport. Resolution : Resolve after Portugal's opening league-phase match in September 2026. The match-winning goal is the winning team's goal that brings its total to one more than the losing team's final total. The answer is the player officially credited with that goal, regardless of which team wins. Accepted Answer Format : The goalscorer's full name. If the match ends in a draw, return “No winning scorer”.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-16 update (BBC Sport & Record.pt Sept 15; Arab News/Al Jazeera Sept 15-16): Wales named their 28-man squad on Sept 15 for the Sept 24 Lisbon opener at Estadio Jose Alvalade WITHOUT starting centre-back pair Joe Rodon (hamstring injury) and Dylan Lawlor (knee injury), plus Ronan Kpakio, while 33-year-old Ben Davies has not played internationally since Oct 2025 following ankle surgery. This defensive injury crisis shifts Portugal's home win probability up (~70% -> ~75%) and lowers draw probability ('No winning scorer' 0.20 -> 0.17). Meanwhile, BBC Sport notes Portugal has not yet named Jorge Jesus's first squad but Cristiano Ronaldo is expected to be selected; local match reports confirm Ronaldo and Joao Felix both started fit for Al-Nassr on Sept 15 and Bruno Fernandes was rested in Man Utd's Sept 16 League Cup tie. Cristiano Ronaldo rises 0.19 -> 0.21 into #1 (discounted modestly for pre-squad/injury uncertainty) and Bruno Fernandes ticks up 0.10 -> 0.11, with Goncalo Ramos (0.07) and Joao Felix (0.06) unchanged (sum 0.62, leaving 0.38 for Rafael Leao, Pedro Neto, Vitinha, Bernardo Silva, own goals, and Wales ~0.08). questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to settle its lawsuit against TikTok over youth-safety claims?
questions.background: TikTok faces lawsuits from U.S. states alleging that its platform harms young users and misleads consumers about its safety protections.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from state attorneys general, supported by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the U.S. state that reaches the first publicly announced settlement agreement with TikTok resolving a state lawsuit over youth safety and allegedly misleading safety claims. The agreement must be announced by September 30, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the U.S. state.
questions.current_reasoning: Major breaking development on 2026-09-10 (Reuters & Texas AG press release): Texas Judge Cory Liu ruled on summary judgment that TikTok violated Texas's consumer protection law (and SCOPE Act) by misleading users about child-safety content filtering and 'Restricted Mode', making Texas the first U.S. state to establish TikTok liability on youth-safety claims. AG Ken Paxton announced the case will proceed to a remedies/penalties trial expected to be scheduled next month (October 2026). Given TikTok's consistent 2026 pattern of settling ahead of trial (DOJ COPPA $400M on Aug 21, three LA bellwether addiction suits on Aug 3, R.K.C. in July, K.G.M. in Jan, and a Kentucky school district case) and Paxton's track record of solo headline tech settlements (Texas skipped the Aug 26 47-state Meta settlement), Texas jumps to #1 favorite at 0.40 (capped below 0.50 since no settlement talks are confirmed and appeal/delay past Sept 30 remains plausible). California rises to 0.15 after AG Rob Bonta told CNBC (Aug 28-29) that California is actively pursuing conversations with TikTok following Meta's $12.2B-$18B multi-state deal (which ties $5.3B to TikTok/YouTube/Snap adopting comparable youth-safety terms). Utah (0.10), Iowa (0.09), and Kentucky (0.08, co-lead of the Meta deal) round out the top 5, leaving 0.18 across Indiana, New York, Arkansas, and ~15 other suing states.

questions.title: Which federal appeals court will next rule that state gambling laws apply to Kalshi’s event contracts?
questions.background: Kalshi offers contracts tied to the outcomes of real-world events. Federal appeals courts have reached conflicting conclusions about whether these contracts are subject to state gambling laws.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Published federal appeals court decisions, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Identify the first federal circuit court of appeals to issue a ruling after August 31, 2026, holding that states may apply their gambling laws to Kalshi’s event contracts. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the federal appeals circuit.
questions.current_reasoning: ZwillGen's 2026-09-15 appellate tracker confirms no federal circuit has issued a merits preemption opinion since the Ninth Circuit's Aug 28 Nevada ruling (KalshiEX v. Assad), leaving only the Third and Ninth Circuits with decisions to date. Crucially, ZwillGen identifies four active pending circuit appeals: Fourth Circuit (KalshiEX v. Martin, Maryland, argued May 7—now 133 days post-argument, matching the Ninth Circuit's ~134-day post-argument cadence), Sixth Circuit (consolidated Ohio/Tennessee appeals Schuler and Orgel, argued July 30—49 days post-argument, after denying an injunction pending appeal in Ohio), Second Circuit (New York Williams and Connecticut Cafferelli, docketed July–Aug 2026), and Tenth Circuit (Utah Cox, No. 26-4100, where the Tenth Circuit denied Kalshi's emergency injunction pending appeal on Sept 8 after Utah won summary judgment on Aug 4), while omitting any active First Circuit appeal. With the Fourth Circuit deep in its expected decision window right ahead of Sept 25 while still carrying ~25–30% risk of ruling for Kalshi (which would pass the lead to the state-leaning Sixth Circuit), we nudge Fourth Circuit 0.45 -> 0.48, trim Sixth Circuit 0.44 -> 0.43 and Second Circuit 0.05 -> 0.04, replace First Circuit with active Tenth Circuit at 0.03, and trim Ninth Circuit 0.02 -> 0.01 (0.01 residual).
